method: Kennard-Stone and SPXY hold-out selection on raw X (no preprocessing), Euclidean distance, start = most distant pair, 15 test samples (test_fraction 0.25 of 60)
source: Second implementation: Python package kennard-stone 4.1.1 (PyPI, MIT, yu9824/kennard_stone), train_test_split(X, sample, test_size=15, scale=False, init='farthest_pair'), run 2026-11-26 in a throwaway environment (uv run --no-project --isolated --with kennard-stone==4.1.1). SPXY: the joint distance Dx/max Dx + |y_i - y_j|/max Dy (Galvao et al. 2005) written out in NumPy in the same script and passed with metric='precomputed'. The package's default scale=True standardises X and its default init='farthest_from_mean' starts elsewhere; both were switched off to match METHODS.md#kennard-stone.

protocol.train_order: training samples in selection order (first = picked first); the package returns them reversed

tolerance.note: Exact: selection orders must be equal
